_readme.purpose: Case blueprint organized by clinical logic (identity, timeline, vitals trend, labs trend, treatment, outcome) instead of by paper page order. Same structure as case_blueprint (3).json, applied to a second case.
_readme.traceability: Every data point carries a source_page field referencing the original page name, so nothing loses its origin even though the structure is now clinical, not page-based.
_readme.privacy_note: Name, national ID, and address are deliberately excluded. Only age, sex, and weight are retained, per instruction, for database storage.
_readme.legibility_note: This source document is far harder to read than the first case (dense cursive handwriting, several pages crossed out). Fields are marked 'confirmed' only when clearly legible/printed; everything else is 'best_guess' and needs verification against the original scan before being trusted.

encounter.admission_date: not confidently determined from scan (handwritten date partially legible, approx. early August 2026)

presenting_problem.chief_complaint: fever and cough for 3 days, failed home treatment
presenting_problem.present_history: known bronchial asthma; reported 3 previous hospital admissions due to pneumonia

findings.note: requested follow-up CBC/CRP; CRP came back negative; recommended discontinuing antibiotic
improvement noted - clear chest, no wheezes, normal heart sounds, good general condition

vitals_trend.unit_notes: temperature in Celsius, respiration_rate in breaths/min , pulse_rate in beats/min
vitals_trend.readings_note: a dense daily vitals table exists in the source (pulse/temperature/respiration/O2 saturation across multiple days), but the handwriting is too tightly packed and overlapping to transcribe individual readings with confidence. Not populated here to avoid presenting guessed numbers as data.
vitals_trend.trend_summary: not available with confidence - see readings_note

flow_sheet_crosscheck.note: used to cross-validate values against cbc_automated_report and lab_request forms

labs_trend.trend_summary: not enough confidently-legible serial values to describe a trend; single-point labs suggest possible early inflammatory response (elevated WBC per pharmacy note) that resolved (CRP negative on follow-up)

during_admission_medications.drug: IV antibiotic (specific agent not confidently legible)

treatment.pharmacist_recommendation: discontinue antibiotic given negative CRP and no clear bacterial indication after reassessment

outcome_summary.hospital_course: admitted with fever/cough on background of known bronchial asthma and prior pneumonia admissions; exam and x-ray consistent with bronchopneumonia; treated with IV antibiotic and nebulizers; antibiotic later reconsidered after negative CRP; chest reportedly clear before discharge
